newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Foreigners buy most of Copel shares.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners buy most of Copel shares.

text.p: Foreign investors acquired most of Copel's eight billion preferred "B" shares, which were sold for 93.5 million reais ($89.6 million) at an auction Friday on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange, a broker said.
"Almost 70 percent of the total shares were sold to foreign investors," said Paulo Vignoli, business superintendant of Banco Omega, one of the brokers at the auction.

Ninety percent of the eight billion shares were sold for 11.70 reais per lot of 1,000 shares, up 30 percent from the minimum price of nine reais per lot of 1,000 shares set by Parana state, the firm's majority shareholder, Vignoli said.

The remaining 10 percent were sold for 11.67 reais and 11.68 reais per lot of 1,000 shares, he added. He said the auction will increase the liquidity of Copel shares, which are seen by many investors as a good investment opportunity in the country's electrical sector.
Banks Banestado, Bozano, Simonsen, Banco Votorantim, Merrill Lynch, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, BBA and ING Barings were also brokering the sale.
